unitTargets: •  I can describe the Big Bang theory and the evidence that supports it.
•  I can explain how the first stars and heavier elements formed.
•  I can describe nebular theory and the steps that form a solar system.
•  I can describe the Sun's layers, activity cycle, and effects on Earth.
keyTerms: •  Singularity, nucleosynthesis, redshift, cosmic background radiation
•  Photosphere, chromosphere, corona, sunspot, prominence, solar wind, coronal mass ejection (CME)
howItWorks: The left column asks the questions you should be able to answer from the notes beside them — use it to quiz yourself later.
A teal rule down the left of a line means must-write. Copy those exactly.
Each section ends with a summary box. Close your notes before you write it.

cues: Put the steps of nebular theory in order.
What has to happen for fusion to ignite?
notes: Describe the process of solar system formation (nebular theory) as a series of steps. Include accretion and protostar and their significance.
*A solar system forms from one rotating cloud — the sun and every planet share the same origin.

cues: Have we ever actually seen a solar system forming?
How do planets end up orbiting roughly in the same flat plane?
notes: Telescopes (like ALMA) have photographed protoplanetary disks around young stars — flattened rings of gas and dust with gaps where planets are clearing their orbits. What stage of nebular theory does that match, and why do the planets end up orbiting in roughly the same flat plane?
